lead.headline: Regional Transit Compact Collapses After Fourteen Hours Of Closed-Door Bargaining
lead.dek: Negotiators walked out shortly before dawn with no successor agreement and no scheduled return date, leaving service guarantees to lapse at midnight.
body: Talks to renew the four-county transit compact collapsed early Thursday after fourteen hours of closed-door bargaining, leaving service guarantees for roughly 240,000 daily riders set to lapse at midnight. Negotiators left without a successor agreement and without a scheduled return date.

The immediate effect is narrow but sharp. Commuter rail and the two express bus corridors run on an emergency schedule funded through the end of the month, while the local routes that carry the bulk of morning traffic revert to a reduced timetable unused since the last work stoppage.

Both governors have the authority to impose a cooling-off period, and each spent Thursday declining to say whether he would use it. A mediator appointed in November has not been formally reengaged, and the authority's board does not meet again until February.

briefs.headline: Senate Clears Stopgap Funding Measure In Late-Night Vote, Pushing The Next Shutdown Deadline Into March And Leaving Three Disputed Agency Budgets Unresolved
briefs.summary: The chamber voted after nine hours of procedural delay, sending the measure to the House with the three disputed agency budgets carved out for separate consideration. Leadership on both sides described the carve-out as a condition of getting the vote at all. The House is expected to take it up Friday.

briefs.headline: Winter Storm Warnings Extend From The Central Plains Into The Lower Great Lakes As A Second System Follows Within Thirty-Six Hours
briefs.summary: Forecasters put the heaviest totals along a narrow band north of the interstate corridor, with ice the larger concern south of it. Utilities in two states moved crews into position Thursday afternoon. The second system arrives Saturday and is expected to be colder and drier.

briefs.headline: Federal Regulators Open A Formal Inquiry Into Automated Braking Failures Reported Across Three Model Years
briefs.summary: The inquiry covers roughly 1.4 million vehicles and consolidates 212 complaints filed since August. Regulators said no recall has been ordered and that the inquiry is the step that precedes one. The manufacturer said it is cooperating and has not received a request for a stop-sale.

briefs.headline: Hospital Systems In Two States Report A Coordinated Billing Outage Now Entering Its Fourth Day
briefs.summary: Patient care is unaffected, but scheduling and billing remain offline at eleven facilities. Administrators declined to characterize the cause beyond calling it a vendor issue. State officials said they were notified Tuesday.

briefs.headline: Ceasefire Monitors Report The First Full Week Without A Recorded Violation Since The Agreement Took Effect In October, Though Both Delegations Skipped Thursday's Review Session
briefs.summary: The monitoring mission credited a local commanders' channel opened in December rather than the formal process. Neither delegation sent a representative to the scheduled review, and the mission's mandate expires in six weeks. A renewal vote has not been scheduled.

briefs.headline: Central Bank Holds Its Benchmark Rate For A Fourth Consecutive Meeting And Drops The Tightening Language From Its Statement
briefs.summary: The decision was unanimous. The removed sentence had appeared in every statement since March and was read by analysts as the clearest signal yet that the next move is a cut. The governor declined to confirm that reading at the press conference.

briefs.headline: Port Authority Reopens Two Berths After Dredging, Cutting A Backlog That Had Grown To Nineteen Vessels At Anchor
briefs.summary: Officials expect the queue to clear within ten days. The dredging ran three weeks past schedule after equipment was diverted to a second site. Shipping agents said rates on the route have not yet moved.

briefs.headline: Parliament Sets A March Referendum Date On The Constitutional Amendment Package After A Committee Deadlock Broke Late Wednesday
briefs.summary: The package goes to voters as a single question rather than the four separate questions the opposition sought. Turnout thresholds remain unchanged. Campaigning formally begins in three weeks.

briefs.headline: Legislature Returns To A Revenue Forecast Roughly Forty Million Dollars Below August Projections, Complicating The Severance Tax Rewrite Leadership Had Promised To Move First
briefs.summary: Budget writers in both chambers said the shortfall does not change the session's calendar but does change the order of business. The rewrite had been scheduled for a first committee hearing next week. That hearing has not been formally postponed.

briefs.headline: Route Reopens Near Summersville After Crews Finish Stabilizing A Slip That Had Closed One Lane Since November
briefs.summary: The Division of Highways said both lanes carry traffic as of Thursday afternoon, with a reduced speed limit through the work zone until spring paving. The slip had added roughly twenty minutes to the detour.

briefs.headline: County Commission Approves A Water Line Extension To Serve Roughly Ninety Households Currently On Hauled Water
briefs.summary: The project is funded through a federal grant awarded in 2024 and a local match approved Tuesday. Construction is scheduled to begin in April. Officials said the first connections are unlikely before autumn.

briefs.headline: State Tourism Office Reports A Record Winter Booking Pace Driven Almost Entirely By Out-Of-State Visitors To The Southern Resorts
briefs.summary: Lodging tax receipts are up in four counties and flat or down in the rest. The office attributed the split to snowmaking capacity rather than marketing. Figures for January close at the end of the month.

regional.item: Cabell commissioners approved a paving contract for the Route 2 corridor at the ceiling of what one line holds.
A Teays Valley water main break closed one lane of the connector through Thursday afternoon, the district said.
Wood County put its courthouse annex roof replacement out to bid with a March completion date attached.
Summersville Lake tailwater releases shift to a weekend-only schedule through the end of the month.

away.item: Village trustees set a March vote on the covered-bridge repair share the select board deferred.
Pender County reopened the south-end beach access after the winter dune push finished early.

fishing.line: 412 cfs and rising after two inches of rain — wadeable only at the Dyer bridge, and barely.
Ocean highs 1:02 a.m. and 1:41 p.m.; water 54.2F at Wrightsville Beach, 25 miles up the coast.

briefs.headline: Ozeki Takes Sole Lead At Six Days Into The January Basho After The Sole Yokozuna Falls To A Maegashira In The Day's Final Bout
briefs.summary: The upset leaves one wrestler at 6-0 and three at 5-1 entering the middle weekend. The yokozuna, who withdrew from November's tournament with a knee injury, is now 4-2. A kachi-koshi at this basho is widely read as the last requirement for the promotion the ozeki has been chasing since September.

briefs.headline: Two Sekitori Withdraw From The Tournament Kyujo With Injuries Sustained In Thursday's Bouts, Reshuffling The Middle Of The Banzuke
briefs.summary: Both are expected back for the March tournament. Their withdrawals hand default wins to opponents already carrying losing records, which the association noted will complicate the promotion math at the top of the second division.

briefs.headline: Conference Realignment Adds Two Programs Beginning With The 2027 Season, Pushing The League To Sixteen Teams And Forcing A Divisional Format
briefs.summary: The schedule model has not been announced. Athletic directors said the divisional split will be geographic. Existing television agreements run through 2029 and are not reopened by the move.

briefs.headline: Veteran Goaltender Announces Retirement After Sixteen Seasons, Ending A Career That Included Three Finals Appearances And One Championship
briefs.summary: He will remain with the organization in a development role. The club has not said whether it will pursue a replacement before the deadline or promote from within.

briefs.headline: Crewed Lunar Lander Test Slips To The Second Quarter After A Propellant Loading Rehearsal Ends Early, Marking The Fourth Schedule Change In Fourteen Months
briefs.summary: Engineers stopped the rehearsal at the eighty percent mark after a valve failed to seat. The agency said the hardware was not damaged and that the slip does not affect the crewed flight that follows. A new date will be set after the valve review closes.

briefs.headline: Researchers Report A Room-Temperature Storage Method That Keeps A Common Vaccine Stable For Ninety Days Without Refrigeration
briefs.summary: The method uses a sugar-glass matrix and has been demonstrated at laboratory scale only. The authors describe field manufacturing as the unsolved problem. Independent replication is underway at two sites.

briefs.headline: Chipmaker Delays Its Next Fabrication Node By Two Quarters, Citing Yield On The Largest Die Sizes Rather Than Equipment Availability
briefs.summary: The company said smaller dies are meeting targets and will ship on the original schedule. Customers were notified last month. The delay pushes the first large-die parts into 2027.

briefs.headline: Survey Finds Groundwater Declines Accelerating In Nearly Half Of Monitored Aquifers Worldwide Over The Past Decade
briefs.summary: The analysis covers 1,693 aquifer systems and finds the sharpest declines in regions that expanded irrigation after 2015. The authors note that a quarter of systems showed recovery where pumping limits were enforced.

weather_ear: Fifteen minutes to the forecast: the Weatherman files at 7:15.
kicker: Fixture edition. Every field is deliberately at or near its ceiling so layout and budget regressions surface offline, not on a news day.
